title: Tech Note: Recovering a Damaged Data File

historical_commentary.text: This note surveys four classic-era techniques for recovering a corrupted 4D data file: using built-in 4D recovery tools, re-indexing, re-saving records, and exporting/re-importing into a fresh data file. Data corruption recovery remains a conceptually relevant practice today, but the specific binary .4DD data file structure and tools referenced are from the pre-SQL 4D 2004 era, and 4D has since introduced more robust logging, backup, and mirroring/recovery mechanisms. related_updates: 4D has since introduced transaction logging, log-based recovery, and database mirroring for more robust data integrity than manual re-indexing/re-saving workflows
